claims.claim: We call the day after today "tomorrow" because our days are numbered in a way that follows a repeating cycle.
claims.note: The word "tomorrow" comes from Old English roots meaning "on the morning," not because days are numbered in a repeating cycle.

claims.claim: When you flip to the next page of a calendar, you're looking at the day after today.
The heart acts like a powerful pump inside your chest.
It pushes oxygen-rich blood all over your body.
It delivers nutrients and oxygen to your muscles, organs, and brain so you can run, think, and stay healthy.
Without your heart, you wouldn't have enough energy to do anything.
A moisturizer helps keep your skin soft.
A moisturizer locks in water so your skin stays healthy and smooth.
Ladybugs eat aphids that might hurt plants.
Scientists study these relationships to help keep our gardens healthy.
Months get their lengths from ancient Roman calendars, which were originally based on the cycles of the Moon rather than the solar year.
The Moon takes about 29.5 days to orbit the Earth completely.
The lunar cycles naturally create a 12-month cycle.
The solar year is actually about 365.25 days long.
To keep the calendar in alignment with the seasons, the Romans added an extra month every few years, creating the 13th month we know today.
claims.note: While the Roman republican calendar did occasionally insert an intercalary month (mensis intercalaris), it was not a standard thirteenth month we know today in the sense described here, and the transition to the Julian calendar abandoned this practice.

claims.claim: February has 28 or 29 days depending on whether it is a leap year.
Electric cars are special cars that run on electricity instead of gas.
Electric cars have big batteries inside that store energy.
When you press the pedal, they use that energy to spin the wheels and zoom you along.
Electric cars do not make any smoke from burning fossil fuels like oil or coal.
Planes fly in the sky because they have powerful engines that push them forward really fast.
Planes have big wings shaped like airfoils that catch the wind and lift them up into the sky.
The biggest planet in our solar system is Jupiter
Jupiter is a giant ball of swirling gas and lightning storms
Jupiter is smaller than some of the super-dense planets found around other stars
claims.note: While some exoplanets are more massive, planets are generally less dense than stars, and stellar remnants or stars are what is being confused with planets here, or else it is factually misleading as gas giants are typically larger in volume than dense rocky exoplanets.

claims.claim: Rhythm is the heartbeat of a song and how it moves and flows.
Beat is what keeps everything steady, like a drum or a metronome ticking away.
Rhythm is all about the music's flow.
Beat is how we keep time together.
Trains are designed to be really long so they can pull a heavy load over a long distance efficiently.
Each car carries the weight of the train and the cargo, which means they don't need to carry their own extra weight.
claims.note: Freight cars do carry their own dead weight and structure, and every added car actually increases the total weight the locomotive must pull.

claims.claim: Longer trains mean less friction between the wheels and the tracks, which helps them travel faster and smoother.
claims.note: Train length does not inherently reduce friction; in fact, longer and heavier trains often experience more total rolling resistance and require more tractive effort.

claims.claim: A pumpkin is usually orange.
Singing in the shower is a tradition to share music with friends or family without worrying about noise outside.
claims.note: People typically sing in the shower alone for acoustic reasons and relaxation, not as a method to share music with friends or family while avoiding outside noise.

claims.claim: Singing in the shower helps wash away soap bubbles left behind.
claims.note: Singing has no physical effect on washing away soap bubbles; water and rinsing do that.

claims.claim: Berries give our tummies energy to play and grow big and strong.
We celebrate New Year's on January 1st because it marks the beginning of the solar year.
claims.note: January 1st does not mark the astronomical beginning of the solar year, such as a solstice or equinox; it is an arbitrary date chosen by human calendar systems.

claims.claim: The solar year is based on Earth's orbit around the sun.
Ancient Romans originally started counting their years from January 1st.
claims.note: The ancient Romans did not originally start their years on January 1st; under the early Roman calendar, the year began in March, and January 1st was only established as the start of the year later.

claims.claim: The tradition of celebrating New Year's on January 1st has carried down through history.
Ice floats because it is less dense than liquid water
When water freezes, it takes up more space
Water freezes by forming tiny bubbles inside the solid structure
claims.note: Ice floats because of the open crystalline structure formed by hydrogen bonds, not because of tiny bubbles inside the solid.

claims.claim: Using public transportation, biking, or walking instead of driving alone reduces your carbon footprint.
Turning off lights and electronics when not in use reduces your carbon footprint.
Choosing energy-efficient appliances reduces your carbon footprint.
Livestock farming is a major source of greenhouse gases.
Eating less meat helps reduce your carbon footprint.
A banana tastes sweet and creamy.
A banana is a big, yellow fruit.
A banana has a soft, smooth texture.
Balloons float up because the air inside gets warmer and lighter when you blow into it.
claims.note: Balloons filled with human breath do not float; breath is cooler than surrounding air and dense with carbon dioxide. Floating balloons require helium or heated air.

claims.claim: Big real balloons can go up really high in the sky.
claims.note: Hot air balloons and weather balloons do ascend high into the sky.

claims.claim: Friends make us feel happy because they share our fun adventures, listen when we have big feelings, and just hang out and laugh together.
Having a budget helps you manage your money wisely.
A budget lets you set specific goals, like saving for a new phone or paying off debt.
A budget helps you avoid overspending.
A budget helps you build financial security for the future.
It is completely normal to feel a little bit scared of the dark.
When you are awake, your brain uses light to tell you where things are and keep you safe.
When it gets dark outside, there isn't as much light around, so your brain thinks it might not be safe anymore.
That's called the fear of the dark.
The fear of the dark usually goes away once you get used to the darkness or go to sleep.
Galaxies are mostly made up of gas, dust, and dark matter.
Gas makes up about 90% of their mass.
claims.note: Dark matter actually makes up the vast majority of a galaxy's mass, not gas.

claims.claim: Dust is just tiny bits of cosmic debris.
Dark matter is mysterious stuff we can't see directly but its gravitational pull keeps the galaxies together.
Stars form from clouds of gas.
Stars shine brightly because they fuse hydrogen into helium in their cores.
Mixing blue and yellow together results in green.
Flowers are colorful things that grow on plants.
Flowers act as little sunshades for the plants.
claims.note: Flowers do not function as sunshades for plants; their main biological purpose is reproduction.

claims.claim: Flowers make us smile when we see them.
Spiciness comes from compounds called capsaicinoids, which are found in chili peppers
claims.note: Capsaicinoids are the family of chemical compounds responsible for heat in peppers.

claims.claim: Papillae are tiny bumps on the outside of your tongue
claims.note: Papillae are visible structures on the tongue, though taste buds and pain receptors are what actually sense taste and chemical irritation.

claims.claim: Papillae detect the heat when you eat something hot
claims.note: Papillae house taste buds and touch receptors, but capsaicin specifically targets thermal and pain receptors (TRPV1) rather than being detected strictly by the papillae as 'heat'.

claims.claim: Your brain interprets this as spiciness
claims.note: The brain processes signals from tongue receptors and interprets them as burning or spicy sensations.

claims.claim: Different types of peppers have different levels of these compounds, which is why some foods are hotter than others
claims.note: Concentrations of capsaicinoids vary across pepper varieties, determining their Scoville scale heat level.

claims.claim: Allergies happen because of tiny things called antibodies in our bodies.
Normally, antibodies protect us from germs, like bacteria and viruses.
Sometimes, our immune systems get confused and mistake harmless things, like pollen or certain foods, for threats.
Some people get itchy eyes, sneezing, or even wheezing when they breathe in certain stuff.
Butterflies fly because they want to find yummy flowers to eat.
Butterflies use their long tongues to sip sweet nectar from the flowers.
Day and night happen because our Earth spins like a giant top.
When part of the Earth is facing the Sun, it gets bright daylight.
As the Earth spins, that same part turns away from the Sun, so it gets dark.
That's why we have day and night every single day.
Rainbows happen because of raindrops.
Raindrops catch the sunlight.
Raindrops bend or refract the light into seven colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.
Sometimes foods smell funny because they have been sitting out too long.
Foods like cheese, fish, and some vegetables can change their smell when they get wet or when tiny bugs called mold spores grow on them.
